target.title: fix(google-meet): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in node host
target.body:
## Summary

- add `outputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` so a destroy(err) on the output process's parent-side stderr Readable cannot leak as an unhandled error event
- add `inputProcess.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `inputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `startCommandPair` so the same protection covers the input process's two stream pipes
- export `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and `startCommandPair` via a `testing` namespace so the new behavior can be exercised by a regression test against the production helpers directly
- cover `attachOutputProcessHandlers` with a real spawned-process test that uses the production stdio shape (`["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`) and a synthetic stderr error, plus listener-count unit tests for the helper

## Why this change is needed

The Google Meet node-host bridge in `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` spawns a long-lived pair of child processes — one for audio capture (input) and one for audio playback (output) — and pipes audio between them. The existing handlers caught `child.on("error")`, `child.on("exit")`, and `outputProcess.stdin.on("error")`, but the individual stdout and stderr streams did not have their own `error` listener. When Node's EventEmitter contract fires (parent process teardown, kernel RST, OS-level EPIPE), the stream emits `error` and — without a listener — that becomes an `uncaughtException` that crashes the gateway.

This is the same pattern that Alix-007 fixed in #101596 (google-meet realtime.ts) for the same extension's realtime audio bridge. This PR covers the parallel surface: the node-host audio bridge, which spawns a different pair of child processes and runs a different code path through `handleGoogleMeetNodeHostCommand`.

## Stream target correction (ClawSweeper r1 feedback)

`startOutputProcess` spawns the output child with `stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`, so stdout is `ignore` and the real diagnostic pipe is **stderr**. The earlier draft of this PR added a listener on `outputProcess.stdout`; that would have been attached to a nonexistent stream in the real process shape and the unguarded stderr pipe would still have crashed the node host on a parent-side destroy. The fix now installs the listener on `outputProcess.stderr` and the test asserts against the real piped stream. The input process uses `["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`, so the input listener targets (`stdout` + `stderr`) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed (1 unit listener-count on stderr, 1 unit listener-count on stdin, 1 real-spawn stderr stream error proof)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: changing the new `outputProcess.stderr?.on?.("error", ...)` block inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new listener-count unit test fail with `expected 1 to be 0`; restoring the block makes the same test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured
in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in
[## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real spawned output
child with the production stdio shape and a synthetic stderr error that the
helper catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: google-meet node-host bridge stream errors on `outputProcess.stderr` and `inputProcess.stdout`/`stderr` no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. Each new listener calls `stopSession(session)`, which terminates both child processes and clears the bridge from the session map.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression test starts a real child via `process.execPath --eval ...` with the production stdio shape `["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]` (matching `startOutputProcess`), waits for the child to write a "ready" marker to stderr (proving the parent-side stderr readable is fully attached), then invokes `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and emits a synthetic `error` on the parent-side stderr readable. The test also attaches a probe listener that records the `error` event firing — without the fix, Node would throw an unhandled error event and the test would fail.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — full file passes, 3 tests:
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper` (~25 ms)
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper` (~1 ms)
  - `catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child` (~50 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper 28ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper 1ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers real-process stderr stream error proof > catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child 58ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The real-process test asserts:
- A real `spawn(process.execPath, ["--eval", ...], { stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"] })` returns a child with a real parent-side stderr readable
- After invoking the production `attachOutputProcessHandlers`, emitting a synthetic `error` on that stderr readable is observed by a probe listener
- The production helper routes the error into the session stop path without throwing

The listener-count unit tests assert:
- `expect(outputProcess.stderr.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stderr error listener is registered by the production helper
- `expect(outputProcess.stdin.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stdin error listener is registered

**Observed result after fix**: the production helper now installs `error` listeners on the real piped streams in the bridge. A `stream.destroy(err)` from the parent (e.g. on gateway teardown) is observed by the listener and triggers `stopSession`, which in turn terminates both child processes and removes the bridge from the session map — the same lifecycle the existing `child.on("error")` path takes.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. The input-process stream-error path is covered by a listener-count unit test in this PR; the real-process proof is focused on the output-process stderr stream because that is the pipe the production stdio shape leaves unhandled.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is the explicit continuation of #101596 (Alix-007 MERGED 2026-07-08) which fixed the same stream-error issue in `extensions/google-meet/src/realtime.ts` (the realtime audio bridge). The node-host.ts surface is a different audio bridge within the same extension — it spawns a different pair of child processes through `startCommandPair` and registers its own listeners through `attachOutputProcessHandlers`. The fix is the same pattern at three more sites in the same extension.

Other active stream-error PRs in the campaign wave (2026-07-06/07/08):
- MERGED: #101394 voice-call tunnel (cxbAsDev), #101402 memory-host-sdk, #101597 matrix deps (Alix-007), #101596 google-meet realtime (Alix-007)
- OPEN: #101598 microsoft-foundry az login (Alix-007), #101599 codex-supervisor stdio (Alix-007), #101846 acpx mcp-proxy (qingminglong), #102047 acp createAcpClient (sunlit-deng), #101506 browser chrome stderr (mikasa0818)

**Collision check**: no open PR found for `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` or for the google-meet node-host stream-error issue. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet node-host" --json number,title,state` and file-level `gh pr list --state all --search "node-host.ts" --json number,title,state`. The only fuzzy hits are #101596 (Alix-007, MERGED on realtime.ts) and #96908 (joshavant MERGED on chrome-node launch configuration, different concern).
